query: Hybrid approaches combining embeddings and LLMs for text/document segmentation (topic segmentation, chunking)
summary: Recent research (2024-2026) shows active development in hybrid text segmentation approaches. Key strategies include: (1) LLM-enhanced TextTiling using embedding similarity, (2) Late Chunking (embed-then-chunk vs chunk-then-embed), (3) Ensemble methods with router LLMs selecting optimal chunkers, (4) LLM-as-evaluator refining embedding-based boundaries. Evidence shows LLM-based methods achieve 10-30% quality improvements over embedding-only baselines, with trade-offs in cost and latency.

key_points: Extended TextTiling uses cosine similarity over LLM embeddings of sentence windows to detect topic boundaries
Implementation combines SentenceTransformer (all-mpnet-base-v2, all-MiniLM-L6-v2) or OpenAI embeddings with TextTiling algorithm
Hyperparameter tuning includes window size (k), pooling strategy (mean/max/min), and similarity threshold
Practical open-source implementation available (saeedabc/llm-text-tiling on GitHub)
findings.details: This approach represents a direct hybrid: classic TextTiling boundary detection algorithm enhanced with modern LLM embeddings instead of traditional TF-IDF. The embedding step provides semantic understanding while TextTiling provides the boundary detection heuristic.

key_points: Late chunking reverses traditional pipeline: embed full document first, then chunk before mean pooling
Preserves global context while producing individual chunk embeddings
Works with long-context embedding models without additional training
Shows superior retrieval performance compared to chunk-then-embed approaches
findings.details: Published in arXiv 2409.04701 (2024). This is not a hybrid of embedding+LLM per se, but a novel embedding strategy that addresses chunking as part of the embedding pipeline rather than preprocessing. Relevant because it shows embedding architecture choices can solve chunking problems without explicit LLM boundary detection.

key_points: Mixture-of-Chunkers (MoC): trains specialist chunkers for different granularity levels, router LLM selects optimal model
Metric Fusion Chunking (MFC): integrates dot-product, Euclidean, Manhattan metrics via learned-layer fusion
Ensemble approaches outperform both fixed-size and single semantic chunkers on QA F1 scores
MFC showed 10-24x MRR gains over naive chunkers in biomedical RAG tasks
findings.details: These approaches use LLMs as decision-makers or routers to select among multiple chunking strategies, rather than doing the chunking themselves. The LLM acts as meta-learner choosing the best chunker for each context.

key_points: LLMs provide sentence-level perplexity or decision-margin scores to identify logical segmentation points
Local minima of perplexity indicate coherence peaks suggesting chunk boundaries
LLM-as-Judge evaluates chunk quality and suggests refinements to embedding-based boundaries
Used in RAG evaluation frameworks (Ragas v0.2, Amazon Bedrock RAG evaluation)
findings.details: This pattern uses LLMs to evaluate and refine boundaries detected by embedding similarity, rather than detecting boundaries directly. The LLM acts as a quality gate or refinement layer on top of embedding-based chunking.

key_points: LLM analyzes document structure and decides chunk boundaries based on semantic understanding
LLMSemanticChunker achieved 0.919 recall vs ClusterSemanticChunker 0.913
LumberChunker (LLM-based) achieved DCG@20 of 62.09 vs baseline 54.72 (recursive fixed-size)
Expensive approach requiring LLM calls for every document, but highest quality
findings.details: This is the LLM-only approach (not hybrid). Included for comparison. Shows that pure LLM methods achieve 10-15% quality improvements over embedding baselines, but at significant computational cost.

key_points: Agentic chunking uses LLM as autonomous agent to organize and split content
Adaptive chunking achieved 87% accuracy vs 50% baseline in clinical document evaluation
Retrieval metrics with adaptive: precision 0.50, recall 0.88, F1 0.64
LLM makes context-aware decisions instead of following fixed rules or pure embedding similarity
findings.details: Japanese sources (Qiita) refer to this as 'エージェント型チャンキング'. The LLM functions as an active decision-maker that can adjust chunking strategy based on document characteristics. More dynamic than static LLM prompts.

key_points: Combines traditional keyword search (BM25) with vector/embedding search
Standard approach in production RAG systems as of 2025
Addresses weaknesses of pure embedding search (e.g., struggles with proper nouns, exact matches)
Both Japanese and English sources emphasize this as current best practice
findings.details: While not directly about segmentation/chunking, hybrid search is the dominant pattern for combining traditional and LLM-based approaches in production. This suggests hybrid approaches are generally more robust than pure LLM methods.

related_topics: Long-context embedding models and their impact on chunking
LLM perplexity as boundary detection signal
Chunk size vs context window trade-offs in RAG systems
Evaluation metrics for text segmentation quality (Pk, WindowDiff, BoundaryPRF)
gaps: Limited empirical comparisons directly measuring 'embedding baseline + LLM refinement' vs 'LLM-only' on same datasets
Most papers focus on RAG chunking (retrieval optimization) rather than pure topic segmentation quality
Few studies explicitly quantify the cost/quality trade-off for hybrid approaches in production
Limited discussion of when embedding-only is sufficient vs when LLM enhancement is necessary
Japanese research tends to focus on practical RAG implementation rather than fundamental segmentation algorithms
practical_recommendations: Start with embedding-based semantic chunking (cosine similarity threshold) as baseline - cheap and effective
Add LLM refinement selectively: use LLM to evaluate boundary confidence and refine uncertain cases
Consider late chunking for long documents where context preservation is critical
For production systems, use router/ensemble pattern: embedding-based for most docs, LLM for high-value docs
Benchmark shows ~10-30% quality gain from LLM methods, but 10x+ cost - calculate ROI for your use case

For kire project specifically: current embedding+TextTiling hybrid is well-aligned with research trends; adding LLM as optional refinement layer (similar to LLM-as-Judge pattern) could be next evolution

evidence_summary.question: Does combining embedding + LLM improve quality over LLM-only?
evidence_summary.answer: Limited direct evidence, but patterns suggest YES with caveats
details: LLM-only approaches show 10-15% quality gains over embedding-only baselines
Hybrid/ensemble methods (MoC, MFC) outperform both single-method approaches
Late chunking (architectural hybrid) shows superior performance to traditional chunk-then-embed
Cost-benefit: LLM-only is expensive; embedding+LLM-refinement offers middle ground
Real-world systems (AWS Bedrock, production RAG) use hybrid search and multi-stage pipelines
However: no papers found directly comparing 'embedding+LLM' vs 'LLM-only' in controlled study
evidence_summary.conclusion: Hybrid approaches are standard practice in production (2025), suggesting practical benefits. Pure LLM methods achieve highest quality but at high cost. Optimal strategy appears to be: embedding for baseline, LLM for refinement/evaluation/routing.
